# Trunk Recorder Pro — building an interface (guide for an LLM)

You are building an interface for Trunk Recorder Pro, a program that records
public-safety radio (P25, SmartNet, DMR, NXDN and EDACS trunked systems, and
conventional FM / AM / P25 / DMR / NXDN channels) from software-defined radios. It runs a web server
(default http://localhost:8080). Everything its built-in interface does goes
through the API below, so you can build anything a user asks for: a
listening page, a wall display, a dashboard, a phone view, a program that
logs or forwards calls.

Read this whole file before writing code. The exact shape of every message
is in protocol.ts (GET /api/protocol.ts); when this guide and protocol.ts
disagree, protocol.ts is right. The human guide is README.md
(GET /api/docs).


## What to deliver

Unless the user asks otherwise, deliver an interface the recorder serves:

- A folder with an index.html, plus any other files it needs: plain HTML,
  CSS and JavaScript (ES modules). No build step, no frameworks, no CDN
  libraries unless the user asks for them.
- Import the client library from the recorder:
    import { TrunkClient, LivePlayer, escapeHtml } from "/api/client.js";
- Refer to your own files with relative paths ("./app.js", "style.css"). The
  folder is served at the root of a port of its own (http://host:8081/), and
  the recorder's API beside it on that port.
- Refer to the recorder with absolute paths: /api/…, /calls/…. Never
  hard-code a port.
- Add an interface.json beside index.html:
    {"id": "<lowercase-id>", "name": "…", "version": "0.1.0", "description": "…", "api": 1, "access": "listen"}
  "listen" (the default) can see and play everything and change nothing:
  setConfig, setTalkgroups, start, stop, quit and the plugin / interface / key commands are
  refused, and the config comes without plugin settings and key sources.
  Ask for "control" only if the interface must change the recorder.
- Tell the user how to run it, in one of two ways:
    trunk-pro --ui /path/to/folder
      Serves it on the next free port for this run (with control) and
      opens it.
    The Interfaces page → Add a folder… (or trunk-pro interface add <folder>),
      then Open. It keeps being served, on a port of its own.
  The recorder serves the files as they are on disk: edit, then reload.
- Make it work at phone width as well as on a desktop.

For a program rather than a page (logging, forwarding, alerts), write a
Node 22+ .mjs that imports a local copy of client.js. Node has WebSocket
built in. Programs need no access settings.

A page served from somewhere else (another machine, a dev server) needs its
origin in the recorder's config: "server": {"allowedOrigins":
["http://host:port"]}. It must import client.js by full URL, and pass
`new TrunkClient({ server: "host:port" })`. Prefer serving from the recorder.


## Template

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>…</title>
<style>/* … */</style>
</head>
<body>
<header><span id="conn">Connecting…</span> <button id="audio">Listen live</button></header>
<main id="main"></main>
<script type="module">
import { TrunkClient, LivePlayer, escapeHtml as esc, duration } from "/api/client.js";

const rec = new TrunkClient();
const player = new LivePlayer();
let listening = false;

document.getElementById("audio").onclick = async () => {
  listening = !listening;
  if (listening) { await player.resume(); rec.listen(); }   // audio needs a click first
  else { rec.listen(false); player.stop(); }
  draw();
};
rec.on("audio", (chunk) => player.play(chunk));
rec.on("change", draw);

function draw() {
  document.getElementById("conn").textContent = rec.connected ? `Recorder ${rec.phase.phase}` : "Reconnecting…";
  document.getElementById("audio").textContent = listening ? "Stop listening" : "Listen live";
  const now = rec.status?.nowS ?? 0;
  document.getElementById("main").innerHTML = rec.calls
    .map((c) => `<div>${esc(c.alphaTag || c.talkgroup)} · ${esc(c.systemName)} · ${duration(now - c.startS)}</div>`)
    .join("") || "Quiet";
}
draw();
</script>
</body>
</html>


## client.js (all of it)

new TrunkClient({ server?, secure?, historyLimit? })
  server defaults to the page's host; in Node, localhost:8080.
  It connects, reconnects by itself, and keeps this state (read only):
  connected   true while connected
  version     the recorder's version
  config      the whole config (Config)
  phase       { phase: "idle" | "starting" | "running" | "stopping", error: string|null, ended: boolean }
  status      EngineStatus while running, else null: { nowS, activeCalls, recording, callsConcluded, systemNames, systems: SystemStatus[] }
  sources     SourceStatus[]: each radio (centerHz, rateHz, dropped, errors, errorPpm…)
  calls       CallView[]: the calls on the air now; [] when not running
  configVersion  the config's version (setConfig sends it)
  talkgroupFiles each system's talkgroup file as CSV text: { shortName: csv }
  history     CallEntry[]: recorded calls, newest first (the last 300 at
              connect, plus each one recorded since; up to historyLimit)
  log         LogLine[]: the latest 500 log lines { timeS, kind, text, time?, level?, system?, site? }
              (after rec.subscribe(["log"]); the recorder's own lines have time (Unix s) and level)
  aliases     talker aliases heard on the air: { shortName: { unit: alias } }
  capabilities  hello.capabilities: what the recorder can do beyond recording
  error       the text of the latest error message (or why a setConfig was refused), or null
  exited      true after the recorder said it was exiting; it keeps
              reconnecting (every 5 s), and this clears when it's back
 Events: rec.on(type, fn) returns a function that removes the handler.
  "change"      fn(rec): after every message. Redraw here. (While a connection is being
                greeted, once, at hello.)
  "<type>"      fn(message) for one message type, e.g. "concluded", "status", "state".
  "message"     fn(message): every message.
  "audio"       fn({ system, callId, talkgroup, samples: Float32Array /* 8000/s */ })
  "connection"  fn(true | false)
 Methods:
  rec.start() / rec.stop()           start / stop recording
  rec.listen()                       live audio of every call
  rec.listen({ talkgroup })          one talkgroup's
  rec.listen({ system, talkgroup })  one system's (its short name) talkgroup's
  rec.listen(false)                  none
                                     (kept across reconnects; one filter per connection)
  rec.setConfig((c) => { … })        change a copy of the config; the whole config is sent
                                     with configVersion. Refused if the config changed elsewhere
                                     meanwhile (rec.error says so)
  rec.setTalkgroups(shortName, csv)  replace a system's talkgroup file ("" for none)
  rec.callUrl(entry, "wav" | "json" | "m4a")   a recorded call's file URL
  rec.talkgroups(shortName)          Map talkgroup → { talkgroup, alphaTag, description, tag, group, mode }
                                     (a conventional system's: its channels, alphaTag the channel's name)
  rec.unitName(shortName, unit)      a radio's name (the user's unit names and the aliases heard,
                                     as the system's unitNames.mode says), or ""
  rec.send(message)                  any command (see Commands)
  rec.close()
new LivePlayer({ followCall = true, quietS = 1.5, gain = 2, onNowPlaying })
  await player.resume()   Call it in a click or key handler; browsers block audio otherwise.
  player.play(chunk)      Pass the "audio" chunks. followCall plays one call at
                          a time and skips calls that overlap it.
  player.nowPlaying       { callId, system, talkgroup } or null
  player.stop()
Helpers: escapeHtml(s), duration(seconds) → "1:05", mhz(hz) → "155.2000 MHz",
  parseTalkgroups(csv), decodeAudioFrame(arrayBuffer), systemName(status, system)
  (status.systemNames[system]).


## The data

CallView: a call on the air (rec.calls, from the "status" message)
  id, system (number), systemName (short name), site? (its site's name), talkgroup, alphaTag ("" if
  not in the talkgroup file), talkgroupOta? (conventional: the talkgroup the air named), freqHz,
  slot, analog, tone, encrypted, decrypted, emergency, startS (engine seconds), sources (unit numbers that talked,
  in order), state ("recording" | "monitoring"), reason (why it's only
  monitored: "ignored" | "unknown_tg" | "encrypted" | "no_source" |
  "no_recorder" | null), patched?, alsoOn? (names of the system's other
  sites carrying the same call; one copy is saved)
  How long it's been going: rec.status.nowS - call.startS.

CallEntry: a recorded call (rec.history, the "concluded" message)
  { path, record }. path has no extension; the files are
  /calls/<path>.wav and .json (rec.callUrl(entry)).
  record is Trunk Recorder's call JSON (snake_case):
    talkgroup, talkgroup_ota? (conventional P25/DMR/NXDN: the talkgroup the air named), talkgroup_tag,
    talkgroup_description, talkgroup_group,
    short_name (the system), site? (the site its copy was kept from), start_time / stop_time (Unix seconds),
    start_time_ms, call_length (seconds of audio), freq (Hz),
    emergency (1/0), encrypted (1/0), audio_type ("analog" | "digital" |
    "digital tdma"), system_type? ("p25" | "smartnet" | "dmr" | "nxdn" | "edacs" |
    "conventional"), voice_mode? ("p25" | "p25_phase2" | "dmr" | "nxdn48" |
    "nxdn96" | "provoice" | "fm" | "am"), nac? (P25's NAC in hex, "293"; "" none), srcList [{ src (unit), tag (its name or ""), tag_ota,
    time (Unix s), pos (s into the audio), emergency, lat? lon? (GPS) }], signal / noise
    (dBFS) / snr (dB) (or null), clean_voice_pct (null for analog), tone_detected, patched_talkgroups?,
    transmission_id (the same on every copy of one transmission saved from a system's sites),
    decrypted / algid / key_id, color_code / ran (-1 none), clock_off,
    tones [the in-band tones heard], tone_patterns [{ pattern, text (in words), signals, … }],
    signals [ids of the system's named signals it carried]
  A call is usually a talkgroup's conversation (its transmissions until it's quiet); a system whose
  recording rules have conversationMode false makes each transmission a call. With several sites,
  a copy the saved one doesn't hold all of is saved too: copies of one transmission share transmission_id.

SystemStatus: one running system (rec.status.systems): the trunked ones, then the conventional
  ones (sites: [], conventionalOpen: channels open now)
  index (the `system` its calls carry), shortName, activeCalls, recording,
  callsConcluded, sites: SiteStatus[], share (shared with the directory: { state: "needsCallSign" |
  "waiting" | "shared" | "error", … }, else null)
  (patches are in decodeDetail)

SiteStatus: one of its sites, each following its own control channel
  index, name (a system of one site: its short name), nowS,
  controlChannelHz (null while searching), identity { nac?, wacn?, sysId?,
  rfss?, site? } (SiteIdentity, as a config site's `expect`: a field not
  heard yet is absent, so test with `!= null`), good / bad (control messages decoded / failed: decode
  rate = good / (good + bad)), modulation, activeCalls, recording,
  callsConcluded, mismatch, radioClock? (the system's clock against ours), callsigns (FCC call signs
  a Motorola control channel sends)
  (adjacent sites, dmr and nxdn are in decodeDetail)

Systems and numbering
  config.systems[]: trunked systems ({ shortName, name?, type: "p25" |
    "smartnet" | "dmr" | "nxdn" | "edacs", enabled, …, sites: [{ name?,
    enabled, controlChannelsHz, … }] }). A call heard on several sites of
    a system is recorded on each and the best copy saved.
  config.conventional[k]: conventional systems. Systems are numbered
    from 0, the trunked ones being recorded then the conventional ones;
    status.systemNames[n] is system n's short name.
  Calls and audio carry `system` as a number (a system, never a site:
  a call's site is CallView.site, by name). Match systems by short name
  (CallView.systemName, record.short_name, SystemStatus.shortName), not by
  position. Talkgroup numbers can repeat across systems: key talkgroups by
  (short name, talkgroup).

Times
  Engine seconds (nowS, startS, LogLine.timeS) count from when recording
  started. Call records use Unix seconds / ms. Frequencies are Hz
  everywhere.


## Messages and commands (only if you don't use client.js)

Connect to ws://<host>/api/ws. Text messages are JSON with a "type".
Binary messages are live audio:
  [u8 2][u16 system][u32 callId][u32 talkgroup][i16 samples…], little-endian, 8000/s.
From the recorder:
  On connecting you get how things are now as ordinary messages, then hello last
  ("caught up": draw the first screen then, and don't treat anything missing as
  missing before it):
  state, config, talkgroups, units, heard, history, radios, survey, monitorEvent, host
  (with control access also devices, keys, plugins, interfaces), then
  hello        { version, platform, api, configPath?, surveyBands, capabilities }
               capabilities: what it can do beyond recording, of "service" (quit, files by path, log,
               M4A), "drivers" (USRP/Airspy/SoapySDR), "plugins", "interfaces", "host", "keys".
               The desktop app has all; the browser build none. Show only what works.
  config       { config, version }: on connecting, and when someone changes it
  configSaved  { version, error? }: answers your setConfig; error when the edit wasn't taken
               (the config changed elsewhere meanwhile) or couldn't be saved
  talkgroups   { system (short name), csv }: a system's talkgroup file (Trunk Recorder's CSV;
               "" none); one per system on connecting, and when one changes
  history      { entries }: the latest calls (≤ 300), newest first
  units        { system, csv }: a system's saved talker aliases (CSV unit,alias,source,time,wacn,sys,tg;
               newest line wins)
  decodeDetail topic decode:<shortName>: { system, channels, sites: [{ index, name, adjacent, dmr, nxdn }],
               patches: [{ supergroup, members }] }
  state        { phase, error, ended }: recording started / stopped
  status       ~2/s while running: { status, sources, load, calls }
  spectrum     ~7/s per radio: { source, centerHz, rateHz, bins: 512 dBFS levels }
  concluded    { entry }: a call was recorded
  log          { lines }: topic log (warnings and errors always); { timeS, kind, text, time?, level?, system?, site? }
  olderCalls   { before, entries, more }: answers the olderCalls command
  monitorEvent { t, level ("info" | "ok" | "warn" | "bad"), kind, … }: something notable (a control
               channel lost / regained, a talkgroup or radio first seen, a radio dropping samples, a disk or
               the RAM spool filling, a tone pattern heard, the clock off…): the kinds are MonitorEvent in
               protocol.ts
  host         every 2 s (desktop app): { t, values (series → value now), platform (os, cores, disks[],
               probes[], clock, …) }
  keys         { sources: [{ name, systems, unlocked }] }: key containers waiting for a password (control access)
  unitAlias    { system (short name), unit, alias }
  error / notice  { message }: about your command
  quit         the recorder is exiting; keep reconnecting, slowly, in case it's restarted
  (more in protocol.ts; ignore types you don't use)
To the recorder:
  { type: "start" }, { type: "stop" }
  { type: "listen", on: true, system: null, talkgroup: null }   ("on" and both fields are always required)
  { type: "setConfig", config: <the whole config>, version: <the last config message's> }
  { type: "setTalkgroups", system: <short name>, csv: <Trunk Recorder talkgroup CSV, "" for none> }
  { type: "olderCalls", before: <Unix ms>, limit: <≤ 500> }   recorded calls before that, from the last 24 hours (listen access may send it)
  { type: "statsQuery", id, series: ["sys/<short>/calls", …], range: "1h" }   history (→ statsResult; listen may send it)
  { type: "radioQuery", id, what: "talkgroups" | "units" | "tones" | …, system: <short name> }   what the
    recorder has heard (→ radioResult; listen may send it)
  { type: "subscribe", topics: ["log", "spectrum:0", "rf:0", "decode:<shortName>", "platform"] }
  A command it can't read (unknown type, a missing field) is answered with an error message.
  (more in protocol.ts: devices, survey, plugins, …)
Listening is per connection. Send listen again after every hello (each reconnect).
system is a system's short name; you get its audio from whichever of its sites carries the call.


## Rules

1. Use field names exactly as given here or in protocol.ts. Don't invent
   fields or endpoints. There is no REST API for calls or talkgroups beyond
   what's listed here.
2. Escape everything that comes from the recorder before putting it in
   HTML: talkgroup names, unit names and aliases come from files and from
   the air. Use escapeHtml or textContent.
3. Never assume a field is set. alphaTag / talkgroup_tag can be "".
   status is null when not recording. Optional fields can be missing or
   null. Show the talkgroup number when there's no name.
4. Audio needs a user gesture. Call player.resume() inside a click handler
   before playing. A recorded call plays with <audio src=rec.callUrl(entry)>.
5. Everything is pushed. Don't poll, and don't fetch /calls/*.json for
   calls already in rec.history (the record is there).
6. Only change the config, or start / stop recording, when the user asks for
   that feature. Do it with a visible control, through rec.setConfig /
   rec.start / rec.stop. Never build a config from scratch: fields left out
   reset to defaults.
7. History reaches back 300 calls at connect, and grows as calls are
   recorded. For older ones (the last 24 hours) send olderCalls { before:
   <Unix ms of the oldest you have>, limit } and read the olderCalls reply
   (more: false at the end). Before that there's no API to list them. Say so
   if the user asks for more.
8. One live-audio filter per connection: one talkgroup, or everything. For
   several talkgroups, listen to everything and drop the chunks you don't
   want before player.play.
9. Keep the page alive through disconnects and restarts. Show the
   connection state (rec.connected, rec.exited); client.js reconnects by
   itself.
10. The API has no login. Don't put the recorder on the internet. If the user
    wants remote access, tell them to use a VPN, an SSH tunnel, or a reverse
    proxy with authentication.


## Before you finish

- It runs from the recorder: `trunk-pro --ui <folder>` → http://localhost:8080/.
- With the recorder idle, it shows the history and a clear idle state, not
  an error.
- While recording, it updates without reloading.
- It survives the recorder restarting: it reconnects and redraws.
- Live audio starts from a click, and stops.
- It's usable on a phone-width screen.
- Every piece of recorder text is escaped.

Working examples to copy from (GET /api/examples/<file>):
  scanner.html    everything, without client.js (the raw protocol)
  wall.html       a wall display with client.js
  talkgroup.html  follow one talkgroup: live, recordings, play new ones as they come
  call-log.mjs    Node: append calls to a CSV file and POST them to a webhook
